rules.summary: Remove repeated transitions where the connection is already clear.
State the fact without announcing its importance.
State the scope or destination directly instead of explaining why this page exists.
Document self-description: check whether this announcement or navigation helps the reader.
Check whether these repeated opening transitions add information.
This clause announces information or endorses a result; state the information directly.
State the supported action directly; preserve its conditions and optionality.
Replace the generic opening with the document's subject.
Consider expressing the action or frequency without this support noun.
The introduction and heading emphasize a count instead of naming the section's subject.
Replace repeated section announcements with their subject.
Check whether each hedge expresses a distinct uncertainty; retain needed qualifications.
State the behavior, scope or evidence behind this quality claim.
Check whether these intensifiers add a measurable distinction.
Consider a shorter phrase that preserves the condition or meaning.
Em dashes exceed the selected local density; punctuation can be intentional.
Several short lists fragment this section; check whether the grouping helps readers.
Check whether this guarantee has conditions or exceptions.
Replace clustered stock metaphors with specific properties.
Replace the cluster of evaluative modifiers with specific properties.
Replace general praise with a specific property or measured result.
Remove a phrase forbidden by this editorial policy.
The ARI formula exceeds the selected level; consider the audience and keep necessary technical terms.
Consider paragraph boundaries while keeping each condition with the statement it qualifies.
This word occurs twice in succession; check for an accidental duplicate.
The definition repeats its subject; state the distinguishing information directly.
This complete list item is repeated in the same list; check whether both entries describe the same change.
This sentence is repeated; consider whether every occurrence is needed.
The explanation repeats a judgment; state it once and name the concrete cause.
The first paragraph closely echoes its heading; check whether it adds information.
These sentences have high lexical overlap; check for repeated information.
This phrase recurs in a short prose window; check whether each use is needed.
Several paragraphs repeat the same opening formula.
These prose blocks have high lexical overlap; check for repeated information.
The predicate repeats the relation already named by its subject.
This clause marks the same relationship twice; check whether one marker is enough.
These passages repeat an assertion; check whether the explanation can be shared.
Several sentences repeat the same opening; consider removing repeated setup.
This summary has high lexical overlap with preceding prose; check what it adds.
Several sentences repeat a POS shape; check whether the structure serves the text.
Remove the assistant's self-reference.
Start with the subject instead of a conversational acknowledgment.
Start with the subject instead of announcing the explanation.
Remove the conversational follow-up offer from this document.
Consider splitting this long sentence without losing its conditions.
Consider a direct verb while preserving the subject, conditions, and technical meaning.
Repeated paired contrasts make this passage formulaic.
Review this common-noun sequence; keep established technical terms.
Check whether repeated paired contrasts carry distinct information.
Review the load of balanced insertions; retain conditions, qualifications, and necessary definitions.
Several sentences contain be-plus-participle candidates; review voice only where the meaning allows it.
Repeated denial and redefinition: review whether both clauses add information.
Check repeated question-and-short-answer transitions.
The contrast names abstract actions without their objects; name the check and its failure condition.
Check repeated triads of evaluative modifiers against specific properties.
Reduce repeated whether-you prefaces while preserving alternatives.
